coverage: Covers the Friday 7 Aug closes. Markets are shut for the weekend, so this is the current live picture.
tldr: THE WEEK TURNED: US July payrolls CONTRACTED 23,000 against ~+80,000 expected, with 103,000 of downward revisions to May and June. September hike odds collapsed from ~55-58% to ~40-44% — no longer the base case, against ~65% priced on 6 Aug.
Your largest risk is now your best performer: silver ripped 3.3% to $63.54 (intraday $65.05) and gold 2.4% to $4,343.43. Silver is roughly +14% from its late-July low, at 1.6x leverage.
GDX +7.10% on Friday, capping a 20%-PLUS WEEK. Your GDX/SILJ/SLVP sleeve — the worst performers on the trend alerts all month — has had its first genuine reversal since June.
Singapore delivered: OCBC record S$2.22b (+22%, first ever quarter above S$2b, loan guidance raised) after DBS's record S$3.08b. The STI is within 15 points of its all-time high.

THE CAVEAT: the bond market refused to confirm. A payrolls contraction plus 103k of revisions moved the 10Y only ~3bp to ~4.61-4.65% and the 30Y sits at 5.20% — fixed income is still pricing inflation. The 12 Aug CPI is the resolution point.
S&P closed at a record 7,757.64, its best week since April (+3.6%). Korea did NOT stabilise (KOSPI -0.60%, SK Hynix -5.22%).

regime.label: Dovish repricing — the hike threat recedes
regime.oneLiner: Payrolls contracted and the September hike stopped being the base case; metals and equities rallied together, but the long end refuses to confirm.

topNews.headline: US July payrolls CONTRACT 23,000 vs ~+80,000 expected — and May/June revised down 103,000
topNews.actionable: The most important input for your book this week. A contracting labour market with cooling wages removes the Fed's justification for the September hike — directly dovish for your levered silver and the miners. But read the falling unemployment rate as cosmetic: it fell because people stopped looking, not because anyone got hired. The revisions matter more than the headline — four months of apparent "stabilisation" were an illusion.

topNews.headline: September Fed hike odds collapse to ~40-44%, from ~55-58% before the report — no longer the base case
topNews.actionable: A regime shift from where your dashboard stood on 6 Aug, when September was priced ~65% for a HIKE. For a 1.6x levered silver position on IBKR margin this is a double benefit — less real-rate pressure on the metal AND a cap on your financing cost. The risk is a violent reversal on the 12 Aug CPI print, especially with ISM Services prices at 70.3.

topNews.headline: Silver rips to $63.54 (+3.3%), intraday high $65.05; gold $4,343.43 (+2.4%), a two-month high
topNews.actionable: Your single largest risk is now working hard. Silver has gone from ~$55.6 in late July to $63.54 — roughly +14% — and is far above the $60 level that was the concern. At 1.6x leverage that is a substantial equity gain in the IBKR account. Consider whether the position size you set for a falling market is still the one you want in a rising one.

topNews.headline: Gold miners go vertical: GDX +7.10% to $89.88, capping a 20%-plus week
topNews.actionable: Direct read-through to your GDX, SILJ and SLVP holdings, which had been among the worst performers on the dashboard's trend alerts. A 20% week does not undo a 38% drawdown from the 52-week high, but it is the first genuine trend reversal signal in this sleeve since June.

topNews.headline: S&P 500 closes at a RECORD 7,757.64 (+0.62%); best week since April
topNews.actionable: Small caps outpacing the Dow says the rally is driven by the no-hike read rather than mega-cap concentration — a healthier mix. Constructive setup for Monday's Asia open, which matters for your HK tech and SGX names after a weak Friday in Asia.

topNews.headline: The long end refuses to rally: 10Y only ~4.61-4.65%, 30Y 5.20%
topNews.actionable: The most important caveat to the bullish week. The bond market is still pricing an inflation problem — consistent with ISM Services prices at 70.3 — which warns the equity and metals reaction may be running ahead of what fixed income will validate. A 30Y stuck above 5% keeps the pressure on Keppel REIT and Mapletree.

signals: The levered silver position has gone from your biggest worry to your biggest contributor in two weeks. That is the moment to review size deliberately rather than let it ride — the position was sized for a falling market.

GDX +20% on the week is the first trend reversal in the miners since June, but it does not undo a 38% drawdown from the 52-week high. Confirmation would be the 200-DMA gate flipping, which it has not yet.

SG banks are delivering fundamentally (DBS and OCBC both records, both raising guidance) AND are the natural hedge against the rate path that threatens the metals. That pairing is doing real work in your book.
S-REITs remain squeezed: the 30Y at 5.20% has barely moved despite the dovish repricing, so Keppel REIT and Mapletree get no relief yet.
Southbound Connect has now sold HK for six straight sessions even as the Hang Seng steadied — the mainland bid behind your Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC sleeve has not returned.
